text: We are fighting for the Cyrillic alphabet to be associated with Bulgaria, Albena Spasova told BTA (04.05.2026 17:27)

We are fighting for the Cyrillic alphabet to be associated specifically with Bulgaria, beyond the popular idea that we are talking about a Russian alphabet by virtue of Russia's large population, as well as fighting to create our own fonts. It was truly important that Cyrillic became one of the three official scripts of Europe specifically through Bulgaria, upon Bulgaria's admission to the European Union. This was stated to BTA by Albena Spasova, a lecturer at the National Academy of Arts (NAA), who on April 22 delivered a lecture in Mexico related to the project "The Letters of Bulgaria – The Alphabet of Europe." According to her, the presentation was structured as a "walk through the history of the world poster," including 30 authors with a leading place in this field. "I had constructed the lecture so that it contained an introductory part about the entire project, followed by two slides for each of the authors, in which, besides the poster for the project, between three and five of their iconic posters were arranged," Spasova explained. She added that within 60 minutes, a "concise but very interesting presentation" was presented, which has already been published on the website of the International Triennial of Stage Poster. According to her, the sustained interest in the project is due to both the universal language of the poster and the theme of the Cyrillic alphabet. "The letter has always been a challenge for the poster artist... this is yet another opportunity to enrich the poster language," the curator noted. She emphasized that the collection brings together "the cream of the world poster," with the works of the participants being part of major international museums.

Participation in Mexico is part of a large-scale international festival in which Bulgaria was a highlight. In addition to the exhibition, expositions dedicated to Bulgarian cultural heritage, rose oil, and tourism were also presented. Within the framework of the event, the Bulgarian artist Gredi Assa was honored with the title of "international honorary professor."

Albena Spasova noted that the event opens opportunities for future cooperation, including the participation of Bulgarian students in international initiatives in the field of posters and photography. She also emphasized the role of the Bulgarian embassy in the realization of the project, describing the presentation as "glamorous and very impressive."

The international poster campaign "The Letters of Bulgaria – Alphabet of Europe," created by the International Triennial of Stage Poster in 2007, brings together 30 artists from 20 countries around the idea of a visual representation of the Bulgarian alphabet as one of the three scripts in Europe. The collection includes 30 posters – one for each letter, determined by lot during the fifth edition of the triennial in Sofia. The project combines the creative efforts of established world poster artists and Bulgarian authors, with one of the letters – "Ь" – being created following a competition among young Bulgarian artists. All works are realized in a unified format and typography and are printed in several languages in a limited edition. The initiative aims to promote Bulgarian culture through contemporary art, turning the letters into a universal visual code. The collection has been presented in numerous international cultural centers.
